title: Dehydration: Symptoms, Prevention, and Rehydration
content:
Dehydration happens when your body loses more fluids than you take in, disrupting normal body functions. Mild to moderate symptoms include feeling unusually thirsty, a dry or sticky mouth, infrequent urination, dark yellow or amber-colored urine, dry or cool skin, mild headache, muscle cramps, and lightheadedness upon standing. In infants and young children, signs include crying without tears, no wet diapers for three hours, sunken eyes or fontanelles, and unusual sleepiness or irritability.

Causes of dehydration include heavy sweating during exercise or hot weather, acute illnesses with vomiting or diarrhea, prolonged fever, or simply insufficient fluid intake throughout the day. For mild dehydration, sip water slowly or consume oral rehydration solutions (ORS) containing balanced electrolytes and glucose. Avoid sugary sodas, energy drinks, and alcohol, as they can worsen dehydration.

Seek immediate medical attention if you experience severe symptoms: extreme thirst, confusion or delirium, rapid heart rate, low blood pressure, inability to keep fluids down for over 24 hours, lack of urination for 8 hours or longer, or fainting.
source_name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
